items_missed: Never asked 'How are you today?' after greeting
No agenda statement setting call structure/length and no explicit 'sound good?' confirmation before diving into move details
Origin address (301 West Avenue) zip code was never captured
Didn't probe special considerations (narrow hallways, tight turns, long walks) at either location
Never asked how many boxes the customer has
Didn't use the 'pricing is super simple' opener before quoting rates

In the estimate, didn't tie stairs/elevator access, the large TV, drive time to the storage stop, or walk distance into the time range, and never used an equivalents reference (e.g. school bus comparison)
Save Your Ass speech only covered the loose-items-add-time point; missing the 'take a carload' tip and a dedicated 'does that make sense?' close after it
Didn't ask the customer to reply to the confirmation email with any corrections
Never gave branch hours or a number/way to reach the office directly
No genuine laughter or personalized rapport-building moment beyond the transaction
top_strength: Calvin clearly delivered three of Einstein's core differentiators (No Worries Damage Coverage up to $2,000, Meet Your Mover, and the On-Time Guarantee) plus a full, transparent clock explanation, and backed the quote with a concrete dollar budget ($1,470) that gave the customer confidence to book on the call.
coaching_note: Round out the Save Your Ass speech with the 'take a carload' tip and an explicit sense-check close — right now Calvin only mentions that loose items add time, so the highest-value prep speech on the rubric isn't landing at full strength; also add the opening agenda statement ('I'll gather some details, then walk you through pricing, takes about 10-15 minutes, sound good?') so every call starts with clear structure.
phone_presence_notes: Calvin used steady warm affirmations ('Cool', 'Alrighty', 'Awesome', 'Perfect') throughout and the returning customer stayed cooperative and comfortable for the whole call, though he responded flatly ('Okay') to her return-customer history and building restrictions rather than warmly acknowledging them.
